note: Rewritten from Sjöstedt's (1900) original description of Termes lateralis, which comprises a Latin diagnosis and a German description; the alate was the only caste known at the time. The description by Walker, based on a single alate from Sierra Leone and transmitted through Hagen, agrees almost completely with the present specimens, and Hagen's suspicion that it is conspecific with E. mordax is refuted by these specimens; figures for wing length, wing width and soldier head width are omitted because of OCR damage, and specimen records are not translated.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head shining, pale reddish yellow, with a few setae; frons produced anteriorly into a truncate, flat-ended tube, the end of the tube with a circular opening whose rim is brown; frons on either side of the tube compressed; remainder of head plano-convex, oval in dorsal view, narrowing anteriorly; mandibles about half the head length, almost straight, apex incurved, straight in lateral view, black, wholly yellow at the base; labrum narrowing anteriorly into a slightly triangular form, with a few setae at the apex; antennae white with pale yellow rings, 12–13-segmented, first segment little wider than the remaining segments, about as long as the second and third together, segments enlarging outwards, spherical or slightly quadrangular flattened spheres; thorax relatively broad, slightly narrower than the abdomen; pronotum narrower than the head, large, oval, sides broadly rounded, anterior lobe short, slightly concave medially like the posterior lobe; mesonotum and metanotum short, the former slightly narrower and the latter slightly wider than the pronotum, slightly flattened anteriorly; abdomen white-yellow, of fairly uniform width, slightly wider posteriorly, densely covered with long setae, as is the whole body; legs short and stout; body length at most about 4.5 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Structure rather robust; head very dark, dirty brown in old specimens, pale yellow in young ones; body white in young specimens, dirty brown of varying depth in old ones; legs also darkening; antennae wholly white, even in old specimens with a dark head; integument thick, viscera not or only faintly visible through it; clypeus very short, narrowly oval, its anteroposterior length about equal to that of the second antennal segment, with a broad semicircular depression above it, deepest immediately behind it, becoming shallower upwards and laterally and ending in an arc; middle of the head with a distinct, pale, small fontanelle pit; two anterior teeth of the right mandible equal and short, the third and fourth teeth very high in lateral view, the third higher than the fourth, the two forming a very obtuse angle; upper margin of the mandibles straight; left mandible very different from the right, first and second teeth equal in length, with a tooth of less than half their length and equally rounded projecting between them, the true second tooth slightly curved downwards, the third tooth triangular and directed obliquely downwards, the fourth tooth very high or long from below upwards, as long as the remaining teeth together; antennae very short, shorter than the head, 13-segmented, the third segment very short and ring-like, sometimes (especially in pale, that is young, individuals) not yet constricted, the antennae then 12-segmented; the first segment barely longer than the three following together, cylindrical like the second; the third segment very short and narrower than the remaining ones; the following segments clavate, enlarging outwards, the terminal segment oval, slightly narrower outwards; pronotum semicircular-oval, sides slightly declivous, anterior lobe short, its ratio to the posterior lobe about 1:3, distinctly notched medially; posterior margin very slightly concave; mesonotum oval, as wide as the pronotum; metanotum of the same shape but slightly wider; legs short and stout, hind femur and tibia equal in length; pilosity sparse but rather long over the whole body.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body dark brown above, with very fine pilosity; head oval, slightly narrowed anteriorly, flattened, slightly concave, with a very small punctiform fontanelle medially; clypeus slightly paler than the frons, not particularly convex, with a fine longitudinal line medially; first tooth of the mandibles distinctly larger than the remaining teeth; compound eyes rather large and prominent; ocelli short-oval, separated from the compound eye by about their diameter; antennae 15-segmented, basal segment about as long as the three following together, segment 3 smallest; pronotum large, almost as wide as the head including the compound eyes, posteriorly semicircular, anterior angles broadly rounded, slightly declivous; anterior margin of the pronotum only slightly and narrowly reflexed, so that the anterior lobe is almost indiscernible; posterior margins of the meso- and metanotum each with two short, rounded projections; wings greyish brown, rather pale, broader and rounded towards the apex; media almost straight, unbranched, rarely forked near the apex; submedia parallel to the media, slightly divergent outwards; basal half of the median area paler; submedia with (10)–12 branches, 0–2 of which are forked; abdominal tergites and the whole remaining venter dirty pale brown, not paler medially; sixth tergite of the female very large, of the same colour as the rest, not or only slightly paler medially; wings pale, with a dirty yellowish brown tinge, short, hardly reaching the apex of the abdomen; terminal tarsal segment as long as the three remaining together. Wing span 12–13 mm, body with wings 6–7 mm, body with head 4–4.6 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Queen: collected on 28/10/1891 from a subterranean nest in a tree trunk, total length 18 mm, width 5 mm, while head and thorax together measure only 2 mm; under the microscope the integument has fine, dense, dark punctation.
